doc.name: A — smartphone case catalogue, snow field, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: translucent MagSafe case
Category: smartphone case
Shot programme: snow field
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You run the tabletop stage for a premium smartphone case product shoot. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the group with variants in a snow field treatment.

SUBJECT. A translucent MagSafe case. Product fidelity is non-negotiable: shape, seams, cap, closure, print placement and colour must match the reference precisely. Only the scene around it is yours to author.

CAMERA. Product with two colourway or size siblings in stepped depth. Shoot on a 90mm tilt-shift at f/16, framing for frame-within-frame using foreground architecture.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with a large overhead octabox with a black flag killing the floor bounce. Stage the product on or against lacquered black perspex, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a punchy saturated candy palette with hard primaries. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Your entire reply is the prompt itself: one dense paragraph, no title, no quotation marks, no trailing notes.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
